newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee market slowed by futures strength.
newsitem.headline: German coffee market slowed by futures strength.

text.p: Recent surges in arabica coffee futures and the strength of the dollar have kept German consumers sidelined, traders said on Monday.
New York arabicas jumped by 18 percent last week, on top of rallies earlier this month, and the dollar is near 34-month highs.
"Roasters are only buying the barest minimum, especially as they fear physical prices have not yet peaked," one said.
The current correction in robustas has not changed this as they are mostly irrelevant for German blends.
The New York March arabica contract ended at 177.85 cents/lb last Friday.
Traders said some roasters had missed their chance to fix prices when the New York spot month was nearer 120 cents in early January and now felt paralysed by the rallies.

Market leader KJS has said it plans retail price rises of two, and possibly four, marks per kg of roasted coffee as of March 10, while others will choose a more cautious approach in order to avoid a negative reaction from coffee drinkers.
"The KJS move is quite bold even though it is completely legitimate on the basis of their (KJS') cost calculations," one trader said.
"They may have taken cover ahead of their announcements in the hope of consumer hoarding before March 10, but the size of the increase remains risky."
Fundamentals would remain tight throughout 1997, with Brazil's crop possibly lower, consumer stocks at low levels and a strike in Colombia hampering shipments, traders said.
In the Northern German import markets, arabica prices were up $13-28 per 50 kg fob on the week.
Brazils were at $189 and Colombians at $210.
Buyers were seeking to replace Brazils and Central Americans with African and Indian arabicas but Kenyan prices were also sky-high.

Traders said Kenyan coffee berry disease and ethnic strife in Burundi were reducing supplies and coffee was snapped up at government auctions at high prices. Kenyan AB FAQ was quoted at $260 per 50 kg, up from $232 a week earlier.
Vietnam robustas were priced at $76 cif February, up $5.
